messages.author: 56b5225107e7c870
messages.subject: using Venn diagrams for faceting
parts:
Is it possible to use Venn diagrams, e.g. as generated by the
Vennerable package, for faceting?
I am comparing several algorithms' ability to detect a particular
property in a set of objects.
I can make a Venn diagram showing in how many objects the property is
detected by each subset of the algorithms.
Now, inside the Venn diagram, I want to replace the object counts with
some graph based on that subset of the objects -- e.g. a histogram of
a certain property of the objects.
So, this is like faceting, except that the object subsets are arranged
in a Venn diagram fashion, rather than in a grid.
Is that possible with ggplot2?
If not, I'd like to suggest this as a future enhancement.

Thanks,

ilya

Not directly, no. However, here is the approach that I would try if I
wanted to do that.

I've not used the Vennerable package, so some of this may be
completely off base. The Vennerable package is based on grid graphics,
which helps because so is ggplot2. I'm assuming there is some way to
get from the Vennerable package the (graphical) coordinates where the
text/graphic should go as well as what subsets it represents.
Separately, generate the appropriate ggplot for each subset (probably
using plry and storing in a list). Convert the graph to a grob
(ggplotGrob). Then loop through all the grobs and place them at the
specified coordinates.

Not pretty, certainly not tested, but at least a direction that might
prove fruitful.
